messages.content: Can you give current weather conditions in Hyderabad?

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve data such as web pages or API responses. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. Must be a valid HTTP or HTTPS URL.

headers.description: A dictionary containing HTTP headers to send with the request.

timeout.description: The maximum number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. A single value specifies a general timeout. A tuple specifies a connect timeout and read timeout respectively, in seconds. This is a float type value.

location.description: The location parameter specifies the desired location for weather information, such as 'Berkeley, CA' or 'New York, NY'.

params.description: Query parameters to be sent in the URL of the GET request. For example, specifying a location to get weather information.

auth.description: A tuple representing HTTP authentication credentials in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem) or a tuple of (certificate file, key file) as file system paths.

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to attach to the request.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be immediately downloaded.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not.

message.reasoning:
We need to fetch current weather conditions in Hyderabad. We can use the requests_get function. We'll call it with url "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast" maybe. But we need to know the API. The tool description says "Query parameters to be sent in the URL of the GET request. For example, specifying a location to get weather information." It includes location param. So we can use open-meteo API. Let's check typical usage: https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=17.3850&longitude=78.4867&current_weather=true. That returns JSON. But the tool expects params dict with location? Actually the params dict has keys location, format. But location is a string like 'Berkeley, CA'. But open-meteo uses lat/lon. Maybe we can use location param? Not sure. Alternatively we can use weatherapi.com but requires API key. The tool doesn't mention API key. So maybe we should use open-meteo. But the tool's params structure seems generic. We can pass arbitrary query parameters. So we can set params: { latitude: 17.3850, longitude: 78.4867, current_weather: true }. But the type says location?: string, format?: ... So only those two keys are allowed. But we can still pass others? The type definition may restrict. But we can try passing location param with city name? But open-meteo doesn't accept city name. Another approach: Use wttr.in API: https://wttr.in/Hyderabad?format=j1. That returns JSON. We can use that. So we call requests_get with url "https://wttr.in/Hyderabad?format=j1". No params needed. Then parse JSON. Provide current temperature, condition, humidity, wind speed, etc.

Let's do that.
